category.title: Prefix Sum & Difference Arrays
category.description: 1D/2D range query optimization, prefix sum + hashmap, difference array updates, prefix XOR, and prefix GCD patterns.

algorithms.title: 1D Prefix Sum Construction (Running Sum)
algorithms.summary: Precomputes prefix sum array where P[i] stores sum of elements from index 0 to i-1, enabling O(1) range sum queries.
explanation: 1. Initialize `P` array of size `N+1` with `P[0] = 0`.
2. Compute cumulative values: `P[i] = P[i-1] + arr[i-1]` for `i` from 1 to N.
3. Any range sum `sum(arr[L..R])` is computed instantly as `P[R+1] - P[L]`.

exampleTrace.title: Trace arr = [1, 2, 3, 4], Range sum L=1, R=2 (val 2+3=5)

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Answers range sum queries in O(1) time after O(N) precomputation.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When multiple range sum queries are executed on a static array.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Financial ledger cumulative balances, image integral images.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces repeated O(N) loop scans with constant O(1) lookups.

algorithms.title: Subarray Sum Equals K (Prefix Sum + Hash Map)
algorithms.summary: Find total number of contiguous subarrays whose sum equals K using running prefix sum and hash map frequency storage.
explanation: 1. Mathematical Core: Subarray `arr[i..j]` has sum K if `prefix[j] - prefix[i-1] == K`.
2. Rearranging gives: `prefix[i-1] = prefix[j] - K`.
3. Maintain running sum `curr_sum` and a hash map `prefix_map` storing frequency of each prefix sum encountered.
4. At index `j`: check if `curr_sum - K` exists in map. Add its frequency to answer count, then increment `prefix_map[curr_sum]++`.

i=1 (val 1): curr_sum = 2. Needed (2-2) = 0 (found count 1!). count = 1. Map={0:1, 1:1, 2:1}
i=2 (val 1): curr_sum = 3. Needed (3-2) = 1 (found count 1!). count = 2. Map={0:1, 1:1, 2:1, 3:1}

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Counts arbitrary contiguous subarrays summing to target K in linear O(N) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding count of subarrays matching target sum with negative or positive numbers.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Financial transaction net zero balancing, analytics revenue target window detection.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) single pass replacing cubic/quadratic brute-force scans.

algorithms.title: Zero-Sum Subarray & Divisible Subarray Sum
algorithms.summary: Find length or count of subarrays summing to 0 or divisible by K using prefix remainder hashing.
explanation: 1. For zero-sum: If `curr_sum` appeared previously at index `first_seen[curr_sum]`, subarray from `first_seen + 1` to `current` sums to 0.
2. For divisible by K: Compute `rem = (curr_sum % K + K) % K`. If remainder was seen previously, subarray sum is divisible by K.

i=2 (val 0): sum=9, rem=4 -> Match index 0! Length = 2 - 0 = 2
i=4 (val -3): sum=4, rem=4 -> Match index 0! Length = 4 - 0 = 4 ([5, 0, -2, -3])

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Identifies contiguous zero-balance or modular multiple subarrays.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When checking for zero-sum windows or divisibility properties.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Cycle detection in discrete differences, parity balance verification.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) hash map lookup instead of O(N^2) subarray evaluation.

algorithms.title: Difference Array Technique (Range Updates)
algorithms.summary: Perform O(1) batch range addition queries `[L, R, val]` on an array, then reconstruct final array in O(N) time using prefix sums.
explanation: 1. Create difference array `diff` of size `N+1` initialized to 0.
2. For each query `add(L, R, val)`: perform `diff[L] += val` and `diff[R+1] -= val`.
3. After processing all Q queries, compute prefix sum of `diff` array: `arr[i] = diff[i] + arr[i-1]`.
4. Reduces range update time from O(N * Q) down to O(N + Q).

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Executes mass range updates in O(1) time per query instead of O(N).
wAnswers.whenToUse: When applying many bulk interval modifications before final reading.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Flight booking capacity reservation, gaming area effect damage application.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N + Q) overall complexity avoiding costly O(N) loops per update.

codeTemplates.code:
def getModifiedArray(length: int, updates: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
    diff = [0] * (length + 1)
    for start, end, val in updates:
        diff[start] += val
        diff[end + 1] -= val
    res = [0] * length
    curr = 0
    for i in range(length):
        curr += diff[i]
        res[i] = curr
    return res

algorithms.title: Prefix XOR Subarray Queries
algorithms.summary: Compute range XOR queries in O(1) time using property `XOR(arr[L..R]) = P[R+1] ^ P[L]`.
explanation: 1. XOR Self-Cancellation Property: `A ^ A = 0`. Therefore `(A ^ B) ^ A = B`.
2. Compute prefix XOR array: `P[i+1] = P[i] ^ arr[i]`.
3. Range XOR query for `[L, R]` equals `P[R+1] ^ P[L]`.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Answers range XOR query in O(1) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding bitwise XOR over dynamic array intervals.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Error correction parity checks, cryptographic range hashing.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(1) lookup using XOR inverse self-cancellation property.

algorithms.title: Prefix & Suffix GCD for Subarray Queries
algorithms.summary: Compute GCD of array excluding one element or query range GCDs using precalculated prefix and suffix GCD arrays.
explanation: 1. Build `prefGCD[i]` = GCD of `arr[0..i]`.
2. Build `suffGCD[i]` = GCD of `arr[i..N-1]`.
3. Max GCD after removing element at index `i` = `gcd(prefGCD[i-1], suffGCD[i+1])`.
4. Precalculation takes O(N log(MAX)) and enables O(1) exclusion queries.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds array GCD excluding specific elements in O(1) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When evaluating GCD metric impact under element removal.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Number theory grid alignment, signal frequency harmonizing.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Dual prefix/suffix technique avoids recomputing GCD across all remaining elements.

codeTemplates.code:
import math

def maxGcdAfterRemoval(arr: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(arr)
    if n <= 1: return 0
    pref = [0] * n
    suff = [0] * n
    pref[0] = arr[0]
    for i in range(1, n):
        pref[i] = math.gcd(pref[i - 1], arr[i])
    suff[-1] = arr[-1]
    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        suff[i] = math.gcd(suff[i + 1], arr[i])
    max_gcd = max(suff[1], pref[-2])
    for i in range(1, n - 1):
        max_gcd = max(max_gcd, math.gcd(pref[i - 1], suff[i + 1]))
    return max_gcd
